title: Local shop, salon, clinic or service outlet
tagline: A physical neighbourhood business — retail, grooming, repair, coaching, fitness — possibly with an online storefront later.
who: Kirana, pharmacy, boutique, electronics or hardware stores
Salons, gyms, tuition centres, clinics, repair shops

structure.why: Lowest cost and paperwork; the shop lives on your PAN; GST only above ₹40 lakh for goods (₹20 lakh for services) unless you want composition or input credit. Incorporate only when you open multiple outlets, take investors or franchise your brand.
structure.alternatives: LLP for partners who want limited liability; franchisors often insist on a company for franchisees above a size.

breakdown: Sector licences: drug licence (pharmacy, ₹3,000–5,000 + pharmacist), clinic registration under the Clinical Establishments Act (state), fitness/salon municipal health licences

timeline: Open the day the lease is signed in most states if you apply for S&E within 30 days; trade licence 1–4 weeks; GST a week if you want it.
taxes: GST optional below ₹40 lakh (goods) / ₹20 lakh (services); composition at 1% (traders) or 6% (services up to ₹50 lakh) once registered if you sell only locally.
Income tax on slabs; presumptive 6% of digital / 8% of cash turnover (Section 58) up to ₹3 crore (₹2 crore if cash > 5%).
Professional tax on the proprietor and staff in levying states.
If your landlord is an individual and rent exceeds ₹50,000/month, deduct 2% TDS (194-IB) even as an individual.
selling: Hyperlocal: Dunzo-style delivery, ONDC seller apps, JioMart partner, Swiggy Instamart ‘local’ onboarding where available
Google Business Profile — free, the single biggest footfall lever
sourcing: Distributors and wholesale markets; B2B apps (Udaan, Jumbotail, Metro) for GST invoices and credit
Franchise: read the FDD-equivalent, royalty, territory and exit clauses; India has no franchise-specific law — the agreement is everything
pitfalls: Signing an unregistered 3-year lease — leases over 11 months must be registered to be enforceable.
Running a pharmacy, clinic or gym without the sector licence because ‘everyone does’ — these are inspected.
Accepting only cash above ₹2 lakh per transaction — section 269ST penalty equals the amount received.
Staff on cash salaries without records — labour inspections under the Codes look at wage registers first.
